posts.text: ADHD don’t care about your pep talks
I built a planner that actually works with ADHD brains — not against them. Because we don’t need discipline. We need dopamine.
ADHD in adulthood is like realizing you’ve been playing life on hard mode with the wrong controller.
My ADHD budget has a section for ‘oops.’
ADHD means is like juggling confetti in a hurricane yet here I am, still thriving.

Your brain isn't broken, it's stuck in the wrong gear. New research is looking at how ADHD brains sync up differently, more like everything firing together instead of taking turns. That tracks with what it feels like from the inside: five thoughts showing up at once, all demanding the mic. It's not a focus problem, it's a timing problem. Your brain isn't lazy, it's got bad traffic control.
